question.text: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 prohibit:

answer.text: Trading in securities while in possession of unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI)
Trading based on publicly available information and analysis
Trading by company employees in any securities

explanation.text: The Logic: Under general securities-law principles in India, the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 prohibit trading in securities while in possession of unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI), communicating UPSI to others (tipping), and procuring UPSI from insiders. UPSI typically covers financial results, dividends, mergers, changes in capital structure, and similar non-public material information. Trading based on publicly available information and analysis is not prohibited. The Trap: Trading by company employees is not blanket-prohibited; only trading while in possession of UPSI is restricted. Trading is also not restricted by time-of-day or to specific market hours under PIT. Note: The detailed PIT 2015 framework (UPSI, tipping, procuring UPSI, public-information carve-outs) is not explicitly developed in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook chapter; the framing above is general securities-regulation knowledge rather than a workbook-page citation.
